newsitem.title: CHINA: China soldiers check their weapons for HK handover.
newsitem.headline: China soldiers check their weapons for HK handover.

text.p: Chinese soldiers are checking their weapons -- and polishing their driving skills -- as they prepare to take over garrison duties in Hong Kong when the British colony returns to China on July 1, state media said on Friday.

In a laudatory article aimed at polishing the image of the soldiers selected by Beijing to defend post-colonial Hong Kong, the official Xinhua news agency said the elite contingent was almost ready for its midnight June 30 mission.

"(The) troops are now checking their vehicles and weapons and are being issued new uniforms," Xinhua quoted Major-General Liu Zhenwu, who will lead the People's Liberation Army (PLA) garrison in Hong Kong, as saying.

The Chinese troops had been issued right-hand drive vehicles for use in Hong Kong, where traffic travels on the left side of the road, but army drivers reared in China -- where traffic goes on the right -- were still practising, the agency said.
"Although the drivers are familiar with Hong Kong traffic signs, they are still working hard to improve their driving skills," it quoted Major-General Liu as saying.
Navy and air force officers had also been preparing for the handover, said the article, which was issued amid a row in Hong Kong over the PLA's first conflict with local officials.
Hong Kong's colonial government said on Friday a dispute between a Chinese general and frontier officers that has prompted widespread debate was just a mix-up.
China has waged a long propaganda campaign aimed at allaying fears among Hong Kong residents over the arrival of PLA troops.

The three-million-strong Liberation Army's reputation in the British colony was shattered in 1989 when soldiers and tanks crushed pro-democracy protests centred in Beijing's Tiananmen Square with heavy loss of life.
China says its Hong Kong garrison aims only to defend the territory from external threats and has rushed to stress the high calibre of its troops.
The PLA garrison would be paid for by Beijing and was even aiming to supply itself with essential provisions, Xinhua said.
"A large farm with a 13-hectare (32 acre) vegetable garden, a 10-hectare (24.7 acre) fish pond, and a modern pig farm has been set up at the rear of the PLA base," the agency said.
"Their food will come from this," it said.
